places.name: Mostar
places.text: Mirna’s home town and the start of every tour: the Old Bridge, the Old Town and the emerald Neretva.

photos.title: The Old Town from the hill

places.name: Blagaj
places.text: The Buna River rises from a karst spring beneath a high rock face, right next to the historic Dervish Tekke.

places.name: Žitomislić
places.text: An Orthodox monastery from the 16th century on the left bank of the Neretva, a quiet stop between Blagaj and Počitelj.
notes: New stop from Mirna’s route: please confirm the text and how long the stop takes.

places.name: Počitelj
places.text: A historic stone village climbing the hillside above the Neretva, with a fortress tower and views over the river valley.

places.label: l
places.name: Kravice Waterfalls
places.text: A wide horseshoe of waterfalls on the Trebižat River, with paths around the falls and the lake below.

places.name: Ljubuški
places.text: A small Herzegovinian town on the Trebižat River. Nearby are the Kravice Waterfalls, the favourite summer stop of the region.

places.label: l
places.name: Mogorjelo
places.text: The remains of a Roman villa near Čapljina, an optional stop on the Herzegovina day tour.

places.name: Stolac
places.text: An old town on the Bregava River with stone houses, mills and centuries of history. Ask about a visit.

places.label: l
places.name: Radimlja
places.text: A necropolis of medieval stećci tombstones near Stolac, one of the sites on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Ask about a visit.

places.name: Jablanica Lake
places.text: A long turquoise lake on the Neretva north of Mostar. Boat tours on request.
places.label: l

places.name: Sarajevo
places.text: The capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina, about two hours north of Mostar by road. Day trips on request.

places.name: Hamam
places.text: The old Ottoman bath house in the heart of the Old Town, where the walk begins.

places.name: Kriva ćuprija
places.text: The Crooked Bridge: a small single-arch stone bridge over the Radobolja stream.

places.name: Stari Most & towers
places.text: The Old Bridge, built in 1566 and rebuilt in 2004, guarded by the Halebija and Tara towers. Home of the divers.

photos.title: The Old Town from the hill

places.name: Kujundžiluk
places.text: The old bazaar street, named after the coppersmiths who worked here, paved with river stones.

places.name: Koski Mehmed-pašina džamija
places.text: The mosque with the best-known view of the Old Bridge from its courtyard by the river.

homeNote: The “What to see” lists on the home map were written from public sources: please check them and remove anything you do not show on your tours.

sights: The Old Bridge from 1566, rebuilt in 2004, with the Tara and Halebija towers.
The old bazaar street of the coppersmiths, paved with river stones.
The mosque with the best-known view of the bridge.
The small Crooked Bridge over the Radobolja stream.
A 16th-century Orthodox monastery south of the city, on the Neretva.
The historic tekke built against the rock, right where the Buna springs.
A powerful karst spring flowing out of a cave beneath a high cliff.
The ruins of a medieval fortress on the hill above Blagaj.
A quiet green river nearby, explored by boat on request.
Stone houses, a mosque and a clock tower climbing the hill above the Neretva.
The fortress tower at the top of the village, with the widest view.
The remains of a Roman villa near Čapljina, an optional stop.
A wide horseshoe of waterfalls on the Trebižat River, with a lake below.
Clear water, mills and quiet spots along the river around Ljubuški.
Stone houses, mills and mosques along the Bregava River.
A necropolis of medieval stećci tombstones, on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
The remains of an ancient Illyrian town on a hill near Stolac.
A long turquoise lake on the Neretva, with boat tours on request.
The museum of the Battle of the Neretva and the famous destroyed railway bridge.
The old bazaar quarter, full of coppersmiths, cafés and ćevapi.
The best-known Ottoman mosque in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
The old stone bridge on the Miljacka, close to where the First World War began.

viewNote: “Look around” uses our photos for now. A real 360° photo (any phone can take one, or Google Street View app) can be added for each place and will turn all the way round.
